To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EB1 is upregulated in early and in field carcinogenesis in human and mouse colon and that the effects of EB1 knock‐down on cell architecture depend on the genetic context.
end‐binding protein 2 (EB2) is upregulated in early and in field carcinogenesis in colon cancer and that the effect of EB2 knockdown depends on the genetic context.
EB1 is upregulated in early and “field” carcinogenesis in the human colon and the nano‐architectural effects of EB1‐silencing in colon cancer cells depend on the genetic context.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the EB1/APC interaction in colon carcinogenesis.
the molecular mechanisms of colon carcinogenesis and the role of EB1 in this process.
the role of the microtubule‐associated protein EB1 in the pathogenesis of colon cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EB1 is an early event, but not a driver of colorectal carcinomas.
EB1 up‐regulation in the colon is an early event, and the cellular effect of EB1 down‐regulation depends on the genetic context.
the role of EB1 in cancer progression is complex and dependent on genetic context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the up‐regulation of EB‐1 is a very early event in colon cancer progression and that EB‐1 is an important factor in the progression of colon cancer.
EB1 up‐regulation in colon cancer is a very early event, which is not only important for tumor initiation but may also be important for the development of the field cancerization effect.
the expression of EB1/APC is up‐regulated during early stages of colon cancer progression and this up‐regulation occurs even in normal colon mucosa adjacent to the tumor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EB1 is upregulated in early colon carcinogenesis and in field carcinogenesis, which is consistent with the idea that EB1 is an early event that contributes to the initiation of colon cancer.
EB1 is upregulated in the earliest stages of colon carcinogenesis and in field carcinogenesis in humans and in the APC Min mouse model.
EB1/APC up‐regulation may be a useful biomarker for colon carcinogenesis, and that EB1/AP is a promising therapeutic target in colon cancer.
